html:
Protests led by students and workers in Beijing's Tiananmen Square from April to June 1989, ended by the army on the night of 3 to 4 June.

They began as mourning for Hu Yaobang, a reformist party leader who died in April. Ten years of reform and opening had brought growth but also inflation and corruption, and the students asked for free speech, a free press and an end to graft. At the height, about a million people filled the square, and protests spread to many other cities. Students went on hunger strike and raised a statue they called the Goddess of Democracy.

Deng Xiaoping and the hardliners declared martial law. Troops and tanks forced their way to the square with live fire, killing hundreds and possibly thousands. Zhao Ziyang, the party chief who had sympathised with the students, spent his last fifteen years under house arrest.

The event is still censored in China. The same year, protests in Eastern Europe ended differently, with the fall of the Berlin Wall.
sum: Protests led by students and workers in Beijing's Tiananmen Square from April to June 1989, ended by the army on the night of 3 to 4 June.
